events.text: The first export cargo of the shale era leaves Sabine Pass, for Brazil.
events.source: US Department of Energy, LNG monthly reports

events.text: The first LNG carrier passes the expanded Panama Canal, loaded at Sabine Pass.
events.label: Panama opens to LNG
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, press release of 25 July 2016

events.text: Drought: Panama cuts the neopanamax draught to 44 feet.
US cargoes cancelled: about 46 in June, 50 in July, 45 for August and 30 for September 2020.
events.label: US cargoes cancelled

events.text: Cold snap in Asia: JKM assessed at 32.49 USD/MMBtu, a record at the time; the Atlantic charter rate reaches 322,500 USD a day.
events.label: Asian cold snap

events.text: Dutch front-month gas rises 16 percent in a day to a record 171.40 EUR/MWh as flows on the Yamal pipeline reverse.
Russia invades Ukraine. Europe replaces Russian pipeline gas with LNG and TTF moves above JKM for most of the year.
events.label: Russia invades Ukraine

events.text: Fire at Freeport LNG takes out 17 percent of US export capacity for eight months.
Terminals and pipelines into Northwest Europe are full: a cargo delivered there sells more than 35 EUR/MWh under TTF on most days.
events.label: Europe's terminals full
events.source: ACER, European LNG market developments, April 2024, paragraph 83

events.text: Gazprom halts Nord Stream 1. The week's TTF average, 83.62 USD/MMBtu, is the highest of the series.
Freeport LNG cleared to restart its remaining trains.
Drought: Panama cuts daily transits to 32. Ships without a slot wait up to three weeks in August.
events.label: Panama drought

events.text: Panama cuts booking slots to 25 a day, then 24 from January 2024, with container ships ahead of LNG.
US cargoes for Asia start to turn from Suez to the Cape of Good Hope.
Red Sea: the last laden LNG carrier has passed Suez; Qatari ships turn south and the route closes to LNG.
events.label: Red Sea closes to LNG
events.source: Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, NG 188, February 2024

events.text: A record 27 US cargoes sail to Asia round the Cape in one month, against one through Panama.
events.source: Platts, republished by Hellenic Shipping News, 22 April 2024

events.text: Panama back to normal operating conditions: 36 booking slots a day, 10 of them neopanamax.
Plaquemines LNG loads its first cargo, the eighth US export terminal.
China's 15 percent tariff on US LNG takes effect; its imports of US LNG fall to zero by March.
events.label: China tariff on US LNG
events.source: Reuters and Bloomberg, in gCaptain, 4 February and 21 April 2025

events.text: The Houthis announce a suspension of their attacks on shipping.
The Strait of Hormuz closes after US and Israeli strikes on Iran. About 20 percent of world LNG supply, mostly Qatar's, is cut off.
events.label: Hormuz closes

events.text: QatarEnergy declares force majeure. Asian buyers of Qatari gas turn to the spot market and JKM moves above TTF; the Atlantic charter rate reaches 278,250 USD a day.
events.source: EIA, Today in Energy, 28 April 2026; LNG Prime, 4 March 2026

events.text: A missile strike damages Ras Laffan: two of Qatar's fourteen trains are out for years.
events.source: Bloomberg and Reuters, in gCaptain, 18 and 19 March 2026

events.text: Golden Pass LNG loads its first cargo, the ninth US export terminal.
The first Qatari cargo since the war crosses Hormuz.
events.source: Bloomberg and Reuters, in gCaptain, 10 and 11 May 2026

events.text: An interim agreement between the US and Iran ends four months of hostilities.
Drought again: Panama cuts the neopanamax draught in steps to 48 feet and neopanamax slots to 9 a day from 4 September.
A Qatari cargo for Poland takes the Red Sea, a rare transit; an LNG tanker is fired on in the Gulf of Aden.
Panama raises daily capacity to 34 slots, 10 of them neopanamax, and restores the 50 foot draught.

parameters.value: 40 percent for 2024, 70 percent for 2025, all from 2026
parameters.source: Directive 2003/87/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/959: Article 3ga, half of the emissions of a voyage between an EU port and a port outside the EU and all emissions at berth in the EU; Article 3gb, 40 percent of 2024 emissions surrendered, 70 percent of 2025, all from 2026; Annex I, methane and nitrous oxide from 1 January 2026. Emission factors and default methane slip (Otto dual fuel, slow speed 1.7 percent, medium speed 3.1 percent): Regulation (EU) 2015/757, Annex I, as replaced by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2776. parameters.value: 51.56 MMBtu
parameters.source: IEA and Eurostat, Energy Statistics Manual, 2004, Annex 3, Table A3.9: LNG, 51,560 Btu per kilogramme, gross

parameters.name: Price of the gas lifted
parameters.value: 115 percent of Henry Hub
parameters.source: Sabine Pass Liquefaction and Centrica, LNG sale and purchase agreement of 22 March 2013, section 9.1.1: 'CSP = (1.15 x HH) + X'

parameters.name: Henry Hub of the loading month
parameters.value: The spot price on the day the month's NYMEX contract expired, three business days before the month, standing in for the final settlement the contracts name
parameters.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Henry Hub spot price

parameters.name: Fixed liquefaction fee
parameters.value: 3.00 USD/MMBtu, owed whether or not the cargo is lifted (2.25 to 3.50 in published contracts)
parameters.source: The fixed fee most Sabine Pass contracts carry (Cheniere Energy Partners, Form 10-K for 2015, pages 9 and 88); 2.25 for BG's first volumes, 3.50 in the Corpus Christi contract with Woodside

parameters.name: Rate
parameters.value: SOFR plus 150 basis points on 115 percent of Henry Hub, loading to discharge, actual over 360
parameters.source: This study: 150 basis points over SOFR, a trading house's short-term borrowing

parameters.name: DES discount, from 31 March 2023
parameters.value: ACER's Northwest Europe DES assessment less the mean TTF front month of the assessment day and the four trading days before, averaged over the last 20 days. It is what the market charges to regasify a cargo and enter the grid
parameters.source: This study, from ACER's method: the assessment is a time and volume weighted average of the deals of the last ten weekdays, and a deal priced off TTF enters at the settlement of the day before it. Its published spread to one day's TTF therefore moves with TTF itself. Here the assessment is set against TTF averaged over the assessment day and the four trading days before: the daily discount is then steadiest (standard deviation 1.7 EUR/MWh against 2.7) and stops following TTF's move over the week (correlation -0.1 against -0.7), 31 March 2023 to 27 October 2026

parameters.name: DES discount, before
parameters.value: 1.25 EUR/MWh under TTF
parameters.source: This study: before ACER's assessments a cargo delivered to Northwest Europe is taken to sell 1.25 EUR/MWh under TTF, the median of the daily discount measured as above from 31 March 2023 to 27 October 2026. The median lies between 1.2 and 1.4 EUR/MWh in every quartile of the gas price, so an amount is steadier than a share of TTF; ACER finds the spread 'closely aligned to the LNG system access tariffs' (European LNG market developments, April 2024, paragraph 86)

parameters.name: DES discount, June 2022 to January 2023
parameters.value: 35 EUR/MWh from June to mid October 2022, then narrowing in a straight line to 6.5 for January 2023
parameters.source: ACER, Market Correction Mechanism, effects assessment report, 1 March 2023, note 69: the difference between the LNG markers and TTF 'was around 35 EUR/MWh between June and August 2022'; ACER, European LNG market developments, April 2024, paragraph 83: the spread 'exceeded 35 EUR/MWh during most days from end-July to mid-October 2022'. ACER, Market Correction Mechanism, preliminary data report, 23 January 2023: the spread between TTF and the EU LNG import price 'hovering between 5 and 8 EUR/MWh during the first weeks of January 2023'

parameters.name: Reported rate
parameters.value: Spark30S Atlantic as LNG Prime and others report it, held until the next report for 26 weeks at most
parameters.source: This study: a reported rate stands until the next one, for 26 weeks at most

parameters.name: Scenarios
parameters.value: Quartiles of the monthly medians of the rates reported for the ship; zero for tonnage already on charter
parameters.source: This study: a date with no reported rate in the 26 weeks before it runs at the low scenario of its ship. For 2016 and 2017 the US Department of Energy's handbook puts spot rates at a third to a quarter of the 80,000 to 100,000 USD a day a new ship needs

parameters.name: TTF in dollars
parameters.value: EUR/MWh x USD per EUR / 3.412142
parameters.source: NIST Special Publication 811, appendix B.9: one Btu (International Table) is 1,055.05585262 J
